statement: The function returns an integer result r (it does not fail), and r equals the number of pairs (i, j) of indices such that 0 <= i <= j < len(s) and s[k] = s[i] for every k with i <= k <= j. Equivalently, r is the number of nonempty contiguous substrings of s that contain only one distinct byte value.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is a lowercase English letter (ASCII code 97 through 122).

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic) on every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is a lowercase English letter.

statement: Let E be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(s)-1 and s[i] = s[i+1]. The function returns an integer result r, and r >= len(s) + E.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is a lowercase English letter.

statement: The function returns an integer result r, and r <= len(s) * (len(s) + 1) / 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is a lowercase English letter.

statement: The function returns an integer result r, and r = len(s) * (len(s) + 1) / 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000, all bytes of s are lowercase English letters, and for all i, j with 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= j < len(s), s[i] = s[j].

statement: The function returns an integer result r, and r = len(s).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000, all bytes of s are lowercase English letters, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(s)-1, s[i] != s[i+1].

statement: Let rev be the byte slice with len(rev) = len(s) and rev[i] = s[len(s)-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(s). The function returns results for s and rev, and count_letters(s) = count_letters(rev).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and all bytes of s are lowercase English letters.

statement: If for all i, j with 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= j < len(s), s[i] = s[j] if and only if t[i] = t[j], then the function returns results for s and t, and count_letters(s) = count_letters(t).
preconditions: s and t are byte slices with 1 <= len(s) = len(t) <= 1000, and all bytes of both are lowercase English letters.

statement: Let n = len(s), and let L be the positive integer such that s[n-L] = ... = s[n-1] and either L = n or s[n-L-1] != s[n-1]. Let t be the byte slice obtained by appending c to s, so len(t) = n+1, t[i] = s[i] for 0 <= i < n, and t[n] = c. The function does not fail on s or t; let r_s and r_t be the integers it returns for s and t respectively. If c = s[n-1], then r_t = r_s + L + 1; if c != s[n-1], then r_t = r_s + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) < 1000, all bytes of s are lowercase English letters, and c is a lowercase English letter.

statement: Let t be the byte slice obtained by inserting c at position p: len(t) = len(s)+1, t[k] = s[k] for 0 <= k < p, t[p] = c, and t[k] = s[k-1] for p < k <= len(s). The function does not fail on s or t; let r_s and r_t be the integers it returns for s and t respectively. Then r_t = r_s + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) < 1000, all bytes of s are lowercase English letters, c is a lowercase English letter, p is an integer with 0 < p < len(s), s[p-1] != s[p], c != s[p-1], and c != s[p].

statement: Let p be the prefix of s of length k, so p[i] = s[i] for every i with 0 <= i < k. The function does not fail on s or p; let r_s and r_p be the integers it returns for s and p respectively. Then r_p <= r_s.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000, all bytes of s are lowercase English letters, and k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(s).

statement: Let l_1, ..., l_m be the lengths of the maximal contiguous runs of equal bytes in s, in order. The function returns an integer result r (it does not fail), and r = sum_{j=1}^{m} l_j * (l_j + 1) / 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 1000 and every byte of s is a lowercase English letter.
